name: Jonah

facts.author: Jonah the son of Amittai, a prophet of Israel (1:1). The book tells his story, and tradition holds that it comes from Jonah himself.
facts.audience: The people of Israel, to show them God's mercy toward other nations

about: Jonah lived in the days of King Jeroboam the son of Joash. God told him to go to Nineveh, the great city of Assyria, Israel's cruel enemy, and to cry out against its wickedness (1:2). Instead Jonah ran the other way and took a ship to Tarshish (1:3). The LORD sent a great storm, the sailors threw Jonah into the sea, and a great fish that God had prepared swallowed him (1:17).

From inside the fish Jonah prayed and gave thanks, confessing that salvation belongs to the LORD (2:9). The fish put him out on dry land, and this time he obeyed. He warned Nineveh that in forty days the city would be overthrown, and the whole city, from the king down, repented. God saw it and did not destroy them (3:10).

Jonah was angry, because he had known that God is gracious and merciful (4:2). The book ends with God's question to him: should He not pity a city of so many people? Jesus later spoke of Jonah's three days in the fish as a sign of His own death and resurrection.

themes.title: God's mercy for all nations
themes.text: God cares for the people of Nineveh, even its children and its animals (4:11).

themes.title: No escape from God
themes.text: Jonah cannot flee from the presence of the LORD, who rules the sea, the wind and the fish.

themes.title: Repentance
themes.text: When Nineveh turns from its evil ways, God turns from the judgement He had announced.

themes.title: A narrow heart
themes.text: Jonah is glad of God's mercy for himself but angry when it is shown to his enemies.

outline.title: Jonah runs from God and is swallowed by a great fish
